sources.role: Not OLMD's code. OLMD's immediate methodological ancestor, used only to recover conventions the OLMD paper leaves unstated (module attach points, zero-initialized fusion scalars, loss weights, BiLSTM per-direction convention, SeqKD distillation, CSLR training and evaluation defaults). Every borrowed convention is recorded as a deviation.
sources.notes: CorrNet (github.com/hulianyuyy/CorrNet, verified in source 2026-09-08) is OLMD's immediate ancestor: it inserts modules after ResNet layer2/3/4 only and fuses them as x = x + module(x) * alpha[i] with self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(3)), which is exactly OLMD's Equation 5 stage coupling with zero-initialized alpha/beta. Its configs/baseline.yaml sets ConvCTC 1.0, SeqCTC 1.0, Dist 25.0 -- identical to OLMD's stated gamma_1=1, gamma_2=25. Its modules/BiLSTM.py line 17 computes hidden_size = int(hidden_size / num_directions), so 'hidden layers to 1024' means 512 per direction. Its modules/criterions.py SeqKD uses KLDivLoss(reduction='batchmean') with logits divided by T and the loss scaled by T*T, and an optional use_blank flag.

runs.repository_commit: 347f55b (plus the working-tree additions committed alongside this entry)
runs.observed: All nine splits parse and match: PHOENIX14 5672/540/629, PHOENIX14-T 7096/519/642, CSL-Daily 18400/1077/1176. Gloss vocabularies independently corroborate the paper's own stated sizes: PHOENIX14 1295 (paper: '1,295 words'), PHOENIX14-T 1115 (paper: '1,115 gloss vocabulary'), CSL-Daily 2000 (paper: '2,000 sign vocabulary'), giving 1296/1116/2001 classes with the CTC blank.
findings: An initial run built the vocabulary from the training split only, giving PHOENIX14 1231 rather than 1295. Corrected to build over train+dev+test, which matches the corpus gloss dictionaries and the paper. The train-only version would have left dev and test glosses unmappable.

CSL-Daily yields 18400 training utterances, not the 18401 names in split_1.txt. Diagnosed in run diagnose-csl-001: S000005_P0004_T00 is listed in the split file but has no entry in csl2020ct_v2.pkl. A defect in the published corpus, not in this loader.

runs.observed: split_1.txt lists 18401 unique training names; csl2020ct_v2.pkl holds 20654 info entries; exactly one split name, S000005_P0004_T00, is absent from the pickle, and no wanted entry has empty glosses. The usable training count is therefore 18400.

runs.purpose: Confirm the reimplemented model constructs on GPU, that shapes flow end to end through backbone, LMA, OMP, coupling and all three CTC heads, that the Eq. 14 loss is finite and produces gradients, and to measure the true parameter count and peak memory. This is NOT the AGENTS.md preflight: it loads no dataset and runs no evaluation.
runs.observed: Forward and backward succeeded. All three heads emit 29 timesteps for a 128-frame clip, above the PHOENIX14 mean of 11.5 glosses, so CTC is feasible. Loss 59.014 (CTC 51.260, distillation 0.310), gradient norm 101.573, peak memory 13.735 GiB at batch size 2 with T=128 on an A10. Parameter count 61.365 M, matching the independent analytical estimate of 61.354 M.
findings: Recorded as attempt 1 of the retained gpu-smoke group. Two earlier probes in this session were discarded rather than retained: a T=32 probe that crashed in max_pool1d (which established the parallel-branch topology) and a run whose return value failed to deserialize locally because a torch tensor leaked into it. Neither informs a terminal decision beyond the finding below, so per AGENTS.md they are not retained run entries.

A first attempt with T=32 crashed in max_pool1d with 'Invalid computed output size: 0'. Two SEQUENTIAL {K5,P2,K5,P2} branches reduce length about 16x, so a 100-frame clip would yield 2 output steps and a 200-frame clip 8, against a mean target of 11.5 glosses. The two 1D-CNNs must therefore be PARALLEL peers over the same features, which also matches Fig. 2's 'share architecture' and Eq. 12's two peer local CTC losses. Recorded as guess temporal-branch-topology.

The measured 61.365 M is 19.4 M below the paper's Table 5 context-9 figure of 80.74 M. That column reconciles with no consistent reading of the architecture (see guess table5-baseline-param-discrepancy), so it is reported as a difference rather than tuned toward.

terminal.detail: Model ran forward and backward on GPU and reported finite loss and gradients.

runs.purpose: The AGENTS.md representative preflight on PHOENIX14: load the exact data format through the real loader and preprocessing, load the intended ImageNet weights, run real optimizer steps with the paper's optimizer and schedule, save and reload a checkpoint, run the real evaluation code on a small dev subset to a parsed WER, and measure throughput and peak memory for the compute estimate.

terminal.detail: The preflight reached evaluation and emitted a parsed metric with exit code 0. All required elements -- real data, intended weights, optimizer steps, checkpoint save and verified reload, real evaluation on a subset -- completed.

runs.observed: Every AGENTS.md preflight requirement was met on PHOENIX14. Real PNG frames loaded through the real loader and preprocessing; ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 weights loaded; 12 real optimizer steps ran with Adam lr=0.001 wd=0.001 at batch size 2; a 703 MiB checkpoint was saved and reloaded with every tensor verified equal (reload_verified true, no mismatched tensors); the real evaluation code ran on 8 dev utterances and emitted a parsed corpus WER; the process exited 0. Training loss fell from 69.186 to 34.280 over 12 steps, a 50.5% reduction, so optimization is working. Peak memory 23.32 GiB on an A100-SXM4-40GB. Wall time 1296.2 s.
findings: WER was 100.0 with 94 deletions and zero insertions or substitutions, meaning the model emitted empty hypotheses for all 8 clips. This is the expected CTC early-training regime after only 12 steps from initialization -- blank dominates before alignments sharpen -- and is consistent with the falling loss. It is NOT a reproduction result and must never be compared with the paper's 17.1/17.2; it demonstrates only that the metric path executes end to end.

The in-function compute estimate of 21.4 GPU-hours for 70 epochs is WRONG and must not be used. It counted training steps only, and its seconds_per_step timer wrapped just the optimizer step, excluding frame loading. The evaluation loop separately measured 50.4 s per clip, about 260x the per-clip training compute; since inference cannot cost more than training, that figure is serial PNG I/O from a network Volume with no parallel loading, not computation. End to end the run averaged roughly 40 s per clip across 32 clips.

Naively extrapolating the measured evaluation cost with a best-dev checkpoint rule (a dev pass every epoch) gives roughly 560 GPU-hours for PHOENIX14 and 1100 for both Table 1 datasets. Those figures are dominated by the I/O defect rather than by the protocol, so run throughput-phoenix14-001 measures loading and GPU cost separately before any compute gate is opened. Quoting either 21.4 or 1100 as the requirement would be misleading.

runs.purpose: Separate data-loading cost from GPU cost, which preflight-phoenix14-001 conflated, so the compute estimate rests on measurement rather than inference.
runs.observed: PHOENIX14 dev clips average 179 frames (range 147-215). Pure GPU inference is 0.0941 s per clip and training forward+backward about 0.194 s per clip. Loading the same clip from the shared datasets Volume costs 27.78 s serially and 15.48 s with an 8-thread pool, so I/O is 165-295x the GPU cost. The thread pool gained only 1.79x, which means the bottleneck is Volume network throughput rather than CPU-bound PNG decoding.
findings: The compute requirement is dominated by frame I/O, not by the paper's protocol. With frames read from the Volume every epoch and a best-dev checkpoint rule, 70 epochs cost about 1895 GPU-hours for PHOENIX14 and 2323 for PHOENIX14-T, roughly 4218 GPU-hours (176 GPU-days) for both Table 1 datasets.

With frames materialized locally so loading is not the bottleneck, the same protocol costs about 22.4 GPU-hours for PHOENIX14 and 27.7 for PHOENIX14-T, roughly 50 GPU-hours for both. The I/O defect therefore inflates the requirement about 84x.

Fixing this is ordinary engineering, not a protocol change: preprocess each utterance once into a compact local tensor cache instead of re-reading hundreds of PNGs per epoch. AGENTS.md directs that ordinary I/O and retry problems be investigated rather than escalated, so no compute gate is opened on the inflated figure.

Even the compute-bound figure of about 50 GPU-hours for both datasets exceeds the 24-hour autonomous gate, and PHOENIX14 alone at about 22.4 GPU-hours sits just inside it. A #repro-sign-team-r discussion is therefore required before any full run, and the estimate brought to it must be the post-fix measurement.

terminal.detail: Measured loading and GPU cost separately and quantified the I/O bottleneck.

runs.purpose: Test the hypothesis that the frame-loading cost is per-request latency across the ~179 PNG files per utterance rather than bandwidth, by consolidating each clip into one JPEG-encoded .npz and re-measuring.
runs.observed: Hypothesis supported. Reading a consolidated clip costs 0.267 s against 6.45 s for the PNG directory in the same container, a 24.1x speedup. Writing the cache costs 0.20 s per clip with 8 threads. The cache averages 1.73 MB per clip at 162.8 frames, so about 11.0 GiB for PHOENIX14 and 13.3 GiB for PHOENIX14-T. Fidelity verified: frame counts match exactly and JPEG q90 costs 1.028 mean absolute pixel levels out of 255 against the same bilinear 256x256 resize.
findings: The PNG baseline measured 6.45 s per clip here versus 27.78 s in throughput-phoenix14-001, because the Volume cache was warm for these six clips. The 24.1x speedup is therefore a conservative floor; against the cold-cache 27.78 s it would be about 104x.

Post-fix estimate for 70 epochs with a best-dev checkpoint rule: 54.7 GPU-hours for PHOENIX14 and 67.3 for PHOENIX14-T, about 122 GPU-hours for both Table 1 datasets. That is 35x better than the 4218 GPU-hours measured without the fix, but still well beyond the 24-hour autonomous gate -- PHOENIX14 alone at 54.7 GPU-hours already exceeds it.

Cache reading at 0.267 s per clip still exceeds the 0.194 s of GPU training compute, so the pipeline remains marginally I/O-bound and further optimization is possible; it would not, however, bring either dataset under 24 hours, because pure compute alone is about 22.4 and 27.7 GPU-hours.
One-time cache construction costs roughly 12.6 h for PHOENIX14 and 15.3 h for PHOENIX14-T, on CPU only, and is reusable across every epoch, seed and both experiments.

Caching is deliberately done at 256x256 BEFORE cropping, so the paper's random 224x224 crop and 50% horizontal flip still vary per epoch. Caching post-crop would have been smaller and faster but would silently remove the stated augmentation, which is a protocol change rather than an optimization.

terminal.detail: Confirmed the latency hypothesis and quantified the post-fix requirement.

runs.purpose: Re-run the AGENTS.md preflight with Temporal Lift Pooling active, timing data loading and GPU compute separately so the compute estimate rests on measurement rather than scaling from an A10 smoke test.
runs.observed: Passed every preflight requirement again with TLP active. GPU step 0.422 s at batch size 2 on real ~180-frame clips; serial batch loading 5.326 s, which is 12.6x the GPU work. Checkpoint grew to 1.34 GB and reloaded with every tensor verified equal. CTC loss fell 57.72 to 20.89 across 12 steps and total loss 71.42 to 25.90. Evaluation ran 8 dev clips in 32.65 s. Peak memory 24.47 GiB. Wall time 124 s, which reconciles with 12*(0.422+5.326)+32.65 = 101.6 s plus model construction and checkpoint I/O.
findings: TLP costs only about 9% more GPU time, not the 2x I had scaled from an A10 smoke test: the A100 GPU step went from 0.388 s (pre-TLP, though that figure excluded loading and so is not strictly comparable) to 0.422 s. The A10's 0.388 to 0.777 s doubling reflected that GPU's weaker throughput rather than the model's cost. The provisional 70-79 GPU-hour range in the gate is therefore too pessimistic and is superseded.

The measured split makes the real bottleneck unambiguous: loading is 2.66 s per clip against 0.211 s of GPU work per clip, so the pipeline is 12.6x I/O-bound as written. As-measured with serial loading, 70 epochs would cost about 317 GPU-hours; that number describes this reproduction's data plumbing, not the paper's protocol.

With the verified JPEG cache at 0.267 s per clip, PHOENIX14 costs about 57.8 GPU-hours (roughly $121 on A100-40GB, 2.4 days) and PHOENIX14-T about 72.3. With cache plus a prefetching DataLoader that overlaps loading with GPU work, the runs become GPU-bound at about 25.5 and 31.9 GPU-hours (roughly $54 and $67, 1.1 and 1.3 days).

TLP's auxiliary regularizer behaves as intended rather than merely running: it drifts down from about 1650 to about 1300 over 12 steps with noise, consistent with the predictor learning to predict odd samples from even ones, while CTC falls monotonically from 57.72 to 20.89.

WER was again 100.0 with 94 deletions and no insertions or substitutions, the expected CTC early-training blank collapse after 12 steps. Not a reproduction result and not comparable with the paper's 17.1/17.2.

measurements.lift_trend: drifts down from ~1650 to ~1300 with noise across 12 steps

runs.purpose: Build a 120-clip trial cache to exercise the cache-writing path and verify fidelity before committing to the multi-hour full build.
runs.observed: Wrote 40 utterances per split, 120 total, 0.17 GiB, in 543.6 s with 16 workers -- about 4.49 s per clip wall. Fidelity verified against the PNG path through the real preprocessing with the deterministic centre crop: frame counts match exactly and the maximum absolute pixel delta is 0.2196 in [-1, 1] units, about 28 levels of 255.
findings: The trial caught a real defect before the full build. np.savez appends '.npz' unless the name already ends in it, so writing to '<name>.npz.partial' produced '<name>.npz.partial.npz' and the atomic rename targeted a nonexistent path: every entry failed with FileNotFoundError. Had this gone straight to the full 6841-clip build it would have read every PNG directory off the Volume, hours of I/O, and written nothing. Fixed by carrying the marker in the stem as '<name>.partial-<pid>.npz'.
The same fix removed a latent race: the original staging name was shared across workers, so two threads building the same clip could clobber each other's partial file. The pid makes it unique.

The 28-level maximum pixel delta is normal JPEG q90 behaviour, not a defect: ringing concentrates at high-contrast edges while the mean stays near 1 level, which cache-probe-phoenix14-001 measured at 1.028. The fidelity report now emits both mean and max in pixel levels so the claim is not resting on the max alone.

Revised full-build estimate from this trial, which is more trustworthy than the earlier 6-clip probe whose Volume cache was warm: about 8.5 wall-hours and $6.42 for PHOENIX14 at 16 cores, and about 10.3 hours and $7.75 for PHOENIX14-T. guesses.detail: The MP-Block remains undetermined, but related work narrows it to a small family rather than leaving it open-ended. Equations 2 and 3 together form the MetaFormer macro-block: a token mixer with its own residual, followed by an FFN of two 1x1 convolutions with normalization and ReLU. Here the mixer is '2D CNNs' over the (T, W) or (T, H) plane. What remains genuinely free is the mixer's depth, kernel shape, whether it is dense or depthwise, the FFN expansion ratio, and the normalization placement.
guesses.planned_resolution: Implement the MetaFormer-style block with an anisotropic mixer kernel following the lineage's long-temporal convention, FFN ratio 4, and Equation 3's literal norm placement. Because the headline mechanism is inferred, any resulting number is conditional evidence and cannot be a produced target value.
evidence: arXiv:2503.08205v1: 'The MP-Block (2D CNNs, detailed in the supplementary materials)'.

No supplementary material exists: arXiv lists only [v1] with no ancillary files, the 9-page PDF has no /EmbeddedFile and no appendix, and the AAAI proceedings entry exposes no supplementary galley. Verified 2026-09-08.

CorrNet (github.com/hulianyuyy/CorrNet, verified in source 2026-09-08) is OLMD's immediate ancestor: it inserts modules after ResNet layer2/3/4 only and fuses them as x = x + module(x) * alpha[i] with self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(3)), which is exactly OLMD's Equation 5 stage coupling with zero-initialized alpha/beta. Its configs/baseline.yaml sets ConvCTC 1.0, SeqCTC 1.0, Dist 25.0 -- identical to OLMD's stated gamma_1=1, gamma_2=25. Its modules/BiLSTM.py line 17 computes hidden_size = int(hidden_size / num_directions), so 'hidden layers to 1024' means 512 per direction. Its modules/criterions.py SeqKD uses KLDivLoss(reduction='batchmean') with logits divided by T and the loss scaled by T*T, and an optional use_blank flag.
constraints_from_related_work: Equations 2-3 match the MetaFormer/PoolFormer macro-block, not ConvNeXt, which uses a single residual and a mid-block norm.
The conventional FFN expansion ratio in Vaswani, PoolFormer, ConvNeXt, ViT and Swin is 4.
C_out = C_in = C is forced, because Equation 5 adds US(X_h) back into a C-channel trunk.

The lineage uses anisotropic kernels with a long temporal extent: CorrNet's spatial_aggregation convs are (9,3,3) depthwise with dilations 1/2/3. A square 7x7 is geometrically implausible on OLMD's plane, which is only 7 wide at stage 4.

Treating a (channels, time, one-spatial-axis) tensor as a 2D image is established practice: the skeleton-image line (Du 2015, Ke CVPR 2017, TSSI, HCN IJCAI 2018, Ta-CNN AAAI 2022), audio spectrogram CNNs, and in sign language SL-TSSI-DenseNet (CVPRW 2023) and SAM-SLR's SSTCN (CVPRW 2021). The R(2+1)D/P3D/S3D/TSM family is NOT precedent: it factorizes into per-frame spatial plus pure-temporal ops and never convolves a mixed time-space plane.

OLMD's Equation 3 places LayerNorm between W_1 and W_2, which matches none of the reference architectures (all normalize before the FFN). Either sloppy notation or a real deviation; Equation 2 also shows no norm before the mixer.

guesses.resolution: Two changes, both ordinary engineering with no effect on the trained model: a JPEG-encoded per-utterance frame cache on the paper's own results Volume, and a torch DataLoader with worker processes, pinned memory, persistent workers and prefetch_factor 4 so loading overlaps GPU compute. The cache stores frames at 256x256 BEFORE cropping, so the paper's random 224x224 crop and 50% horizontal flip still vary every epoch; per-item RNG is seeded by (seed, index) so worker processes do not share augmentation state and runs stay repeatable. Padding replicates the last frame rather than using zeros, because LMA differences each frame against its neighbours and zero padding would make boundary differences spuriously large.
